Hi Alyssa,

Thanks again for the intro call this morning — appreciate the context on your patient-facing summarization and triage workflows. Quick recap and asks so we can turn this into a short estimate for procurement: 

What I captured:
- Primary workload: discharge summaries + patient message reply suggestions (high-quality generation; safety filters)
- Expected steady-state usage: target ~8–12M tokens/month in Q2 with spike months up to ~18M
- Latency requirement: 200–400ms p50 for generation flows, occasional background batch jobs OK at higher SLAs
- Data controls: VPC + SOC2 logs required; see our Private offering note if needed

Pricing info we need from you to refine the estimate: 
1) Target budget range for hosted inference (monthly run-rate) — helps us choose model/quantization tradeoffs (e.g., $/1M tokens target).
2) Whether you need reserved throughput (Guaranteed lanes) vs. best-effort burstable capacity for spikes.
3) Any procurement timing constraints (PO timeline / contract window).

Next steps I propose: 
- Marcus (cc’d) will assemble a short cost model with three scenarios (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) including unit $/1M tokens and an invoice-style estimate.
- If you can reply with budget range and whether procurement prefers monthly or annual billing, we’ll finalize a PDF estimate for legal/procurement.

If helpful, happy to lock a 30-min follow-up later this week to walk the scenarios.

Thanks,

Hi Alyssa / Vanessa,

Per Vanessa’s notes, I’ve put together a compact cost model (attached) and a one-page invoice-style estimate. High-level summary below — see attached spreadsheet (NIM-Cost-Model-v1.xlsx) and quick CSV for token breakdown.

Attached artifacts:
- NIM-Cost-Model-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — scenario tabs + assumptions
- estimate-2026-03-10.pdf (pdf) — one-page invoice-style estimate for procurement
- scenarios-token-breakdown.csv (csv) — month-by-month token ramp used in the model

Key assumptions used across scenarios:
- Model family: medium-capacity open decoder (quantized 4-bit) suitable for high-quality generation with safety filters enabled.
- Average tokens per generation: 280 tokens (prompt + response amortized)
- KV cache savings assumed for steady-state conversation flows (~15% token reduction after warm-up)
- Support/observability: standard Console access + 30-day traces (included)

Scenario summaries (monthly cost / $ per 1M tokens):
- Conservative (low-cost): $9,300 / $775 per 1M tokens — higher batching, aggressive quantization, best-effort reserved capacity (suitable if you accept slightly higher p99).
- Balanced (recommended): $13,800 / $1,150 per 1M tokens — balanced throughput/latency, modest reserved lanes for UI flows, moderate quantization (good quality/price mix).
- Aggressive (low-latency, premium): $20,500 / $1,700 per 1M tokens — more reserved throughput, higher performance kernels, dedicated capacity to meet tight p99s.

Notes and options: 
- If you commit to 12-month reserved capacity we can drop the Balanced $/1M to ~$980 (preliminary) — I included a reserve-commitment tab in the spreadsheet with commit tiers.
- We included a line item for SOC2 + VPC connector in the invoice as an optional one-time setup fee (listed separately).
- The estimate PDF is formatted for procurement; if you prefer annual pricing we can convert the figures to an annual committed quote with an attached SOW stub.

Requested next steps: 
1) Please confirm which scenario you want us to convert to a formal quote and whether procurement prefers monthly or annual billing.
2) If you want, schedule a 30-min walkthrough and I’ll screen-share the spreadsheet and assumptions.

I’ll also flag this to Rachel to coordinate any discount approvals.

—Marcus Lin
